about.title: Larkspur Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Larkspur's mix of small retail centers, hillside walkways, and older apartment buildings creates plenty of spots where a wet floor, cracked pavement, loose stair tread, or poor lighting can cause a serious fall. Whether it happened along the Sir Francis Drake Boulevard corridor, in a lot off Magnolia Avenue, or inside a business near US-101, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have reasonably known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That's the heart of a premises liability claim here. Because evidence like surveillance footage, maintenance logs, and incident reports can disappear quickly, early documentation matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options under California's comparative fault rules.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California premises law requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney knows how to dig up prior complaints, work orders, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Larkspur businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: Because California applies pure comparative fault, a property owner's team may try to shift blame onto you. An attorney can push back and make sure your share of responsibility, if any, is fairly and accurately assessed.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Larkspur?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California's statute of limitations. If a government-owned property was involved, such as a public sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Speaking with someone quickly helps avoid missing either window.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some responsibility for the fall. Your potential recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how that split might realistically play out.

items.question: Does it matter that Larkspur crashes and falls both cluster on busy days?
items.answer: Local data shows crash reports around Larkspur tend to peak Friday afternoons, which often coincides with heavier foot traffic at shops and lots along Magnolia Avenue and Sir Francis Drake Boulevard. Higher pedestrian volume on those days can mean more spills, debris, or crowding go unaddressed. That pattern can be useful context when reconstructing how and why a hazard was allowed to exist.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Photograph the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries before anything changes or gets cleaned up. Ask the property to preserve any surveillance video and get contact information for witnesses if possible. Then consider getting a free case review so an independent attorney can advise you on next steps.
